items.title: Northern Ontario Braces for 20 cm of Snow While GTA and Niagara Get a Mild, Sunny Sunday
items.summary: According to Environment Canada, while northern Ontario braces for up to 20 centimetres of snow, the GTA and Niagara region are set for an unseasonably mild and sunny Sunday. The forecaster says Saturday night will stay clear across the region, with patches of fog developing overnight. Lows are expected to dip to around 5 C in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington, and 7 C in Durham and Niagara. Environment Canada forecasts a high of 14 C for Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington, with Durham reaching 15 C and Niagara warming to 16 C under south winds. Clouds are expected to move in Sunday night, bringing a 30 per cent chance of showers to most areas. The agency says winds will shift northwest overnight, gusting as high as 50 km/h in the western GTA. Drivers are warned to watch for fog early Sunday morning, which could reduce visibility on roads.

items.title: Hurontario Street Shut Down for Hours After Two-Vehicle Crash Leaves Woman with Serious Injuries
items.summary: According to Peel police, a woman was taken to a trauma centre with serious injuries after a two-vehicle crash in Mississauga on Saturday afternoon, Nov. 21. Police say a male driver involved in the same crash was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries. Southbound Hurontario Street was closed between Eglinton Avenue and Elia Avenue while officers investigated, according to police. Drivers were asked to seek alternate routes during the closure. Police have not said what caused the crash or whether charges are expected. Hurontario Street is one of Mississauga's busiest roads, running north to south through the city, and the Eglinton intersection is one of its main crossings. Police are asking anyone with information or dashcam footage to contact them and quote occurrence number PR260394750, or reach Crime Stoppers anonymously.

items.title: Mississauga Arts Council Honours Billy Talent for 15 Years Backing Mental Health Charity Make Music Matter
items.summary: According to CBC Peel, the Mississauga Arts Council presented Billy Talent with an award this week recognizing the punk rock band's work beyond its music career. The council says the honour reflects the band's long-running support for Make Music Matter, a mental health charity the group has backed for 15 years. CBC Peel reports the charity uses songwriting as a therapeutic tool meant to empower and help heal people. Host Nav Nanwa covered the recognition for CBC Peel. The award highlights local artists whose community contributions extend past their creative output, according to the broadcaster.

items.title: Church Street Reopens After Vehicle Strikes and Seriously Injures Pedestrian in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Peel police, a pedestrian was seriously injured after being struck by a vehicle in Mississauga. Police say the pedestrian was taken to a local hospital with serious injuries following the collision. The driver remained at the scene after the crash, according to police. Officers temporarily closed Church Street between Old Pine Street and Main Street while emergency crews responded to the scene. Police say the intersection has since reopened to traffic. No further details about the pedestrian's condition were immediately available.

items.title: Officers Misjudged Jamal Francique's Walking Pace Before Arrest Turned Into Takedown, Inquest Told
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the police shooting death of Jamal Francique, Peel Regional Police detective Jason Sweeting said officers failed to anticipate several factors in their 2020 arrest plan, including Francique's prior victimization. Sweeting testified that Francique walked from his home to his car faster than officers expected, delaying their response. Police had planned to block Francique's vehicle with an unmarked car once he reached it, believing they could arrest him first, according to the inquest. Instead, the operation turned into a high risk takedown after Francique entered his vehicle and put it into motion, the inquest heard. The shooting took place outside a townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020. The inquest also heard there was no urgency to rush the arrest, since Francique had only breached bail conditions days earlier.

items.title: Cedar Tree Circles, Didukh-Making and Mocktail Classes Headline CreativeHub 1352's December Workshop Lineup
items.summary: According to CreativeHub 1352, a new slate of hands-on workshops will run alongside the Mississauga Festival of Trees at the Small Arms Inspection Building from Dec. 4 to 13. The non-profit says the lineup includes an Indigenous Cedar Tree Circle, a session on the Ukrainian tradition of Didukh-making, and a candle-making class. Organizers say other sessions let participants try soft pastels, acrylic painting, needle felting, embroidery and letter writing. CreativeHub 1352 says wellness options are also on offer, including morning yoga, a clarifying face mask workshop and a tasting of Himalayan tartary buckwheat. The group says a mocktail-making class is included too, with proceeds supporting its non-profit programming. CreativeHub 1352 notes free drop-in activities will run throughout the festival for anyone who prefers not to register in advance.

items.title: Local Taxpayers Cover Services Gap as Advocates Say Ontario Shortchanges Peel Non-Profits by $1.4 Billion
items.summary: According to Metamorphosis Network coordinator Sean Meagher, Ontario is underfunding non-profits across Mississauga, Brampton and the wider GTA by roughly $1.4 billion, spanning housing, long-term care and addiction services. Meagher told insauga.com funding outside Toronto has not kept pace with demand, and that the Peel shortfall alone stood at $868 million a year as of 2024. He said Metamorphosis data showed the province gives Peel residents $578 less per person annually than comparable regions, noting Toronto is twice Peel's size yet has six times the affordable housing. Meagher said a gap in one area ripples across the system, with local taxpayers covering costs the province should bear. He added that in York Region, that gap rose by $123 million over the past decade. Meagher said roughly 10 per cent of a resident's tax bill funds services the province should cover.
